ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AD$ is the median of $\triangle ABC$. If $AB=AC=13$ and $BC=10$, then what is the length of $AD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $AD$ is the median of $\triangle ABC$, if $AB=AC=13$, $BC=10$, \\
then $AD\perp BC$, $BD=\frac{1}{2}BC=5$, \\
In $Rt\triangle ABD$, by the Pythagorean theorem, we have: $AD=\sqrt{AB^{2}-BD^{2}}=\boxed{12}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AD$ is the median of $\triangle ABC$. If $AB=AC=13$ and $BC=10$, then what is the length of $AD$?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: In the image, vertex A of triangle ABC is above, and B and C are below forming base BC; point D is located on BC, and line segment AD connects from A to D on the base. The problem states that AD is the median of triangle ABC, so D is the midpoint of BC. Because BC=10, BD=DC=5. Also because AB=AC=13, triangle ABC is an isosceles triangle; the median from the vertex angle of an isosceles triangle to the base is also perpendicular to the base, so AD is perpendicular to BC, and triangle ABD is a right triangle. In right triangle ABD, AB=13 is the hypotenuse, and BD=5 is a leg; by the Pythagorean theorem, AD=sqrt(13^2-5^2)=sqrt(169-25)=sqrt(144)=12.
